reviewedRevision: 59e0039 plus the rework in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request: the known 3-stage shortfall went straight to a retrofit, followed by one independent review round. Its two MEDIUM findings were fixed and verified by re-running the reviewer's own rules and touch probe, one clean-worktree run and the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: The reviewer's own goal-aware player, reading only public state, cleared 99.9% of runs (40 seeds on each of 20 gardens, every garden at least 98%, median 11-22 moves to spare); a goal-blind high-score player cleared 96.5%. From garden 3, random legal swaps cleared 8.1% overall (at most 18% on a garden), repeating the first legal swap 0%, and pointer mashing at most 19% at 150 seeds, all under the 25% cap. No accepted swap failed to match, no rejected swap cost a move, cascade scores were always exact, a dead board remixed for free, and fuzz, determinism at 30, 60 and 120 Hz and broken progress stores all passed. On the final files the same rules probe reported 0 violations and 0 fuzz throws, and its drag from one gem to the next ended in a swap.

findings.observation: Only 3 stages with per-stage goal logic and no select or continue. There are now 20 data-driven gardens with score, collect, coloured soil-bed and combined goals under move budgets, accurate EN/ZH tips, a garden select and env.progress continue; dead boards remix for free, and the 805-line file is split into six modules.

Review finding: touch only supported tap-then-tap. Pressing a gem and releasing past it now swaps with the neighbour in the dominant drag direction; tap-tap still works and the help text mentions dragging.

Review finding: soil beds showed their required gem only by colour, Rose and Leaf were close under red-green colour blindness, and Rose and Dew shared a silhouette. Every gem kind now has its own shape, and each bed carries a badge with the wanted gem's shape as well as its colour.
Garden 20 now shows as cleared after the final win, and the fallback board respects the garden's gem kinds.

openNotes: The bed shape badge is about 11 px on the 480 px canvas, small on a phone.
The game is generous: a sensible player finishes most gardens with many moves to spare.
A press and move that both land within a single frame read as a tap at the release point; a real finger drag spans several frames.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start, Resume and the board, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read, except that garden 3 was rendered from the game's own modules into a separate canvas to inspect the bed badges.
observed: Chinese: Start opened garden 1 of 20 (育苗床, score 1500 in 20 moves) with the tip below the board; all four gem kinds have distinct silhouettes.
Tap then tap on adjacent gems swapped them, matched four and cascaded (score 280, 19 moves left).
The automation tool's drag pressed, moved and released within one frame, which the game read as a tap at the release cell; the frame-stepped probe confirms that a real drag swaps.
Garden 3 rendered with a shape badge in the top-left corner of every soil bed (leaf, drop, sun, rose) beside the coloured corner marks.
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): six touch buttons (向左 向右 向上 向下 选择/下一关 提示); the select button picked the gem under the cursor.
Not covered in the browser: a garden win or loss and the garden select; the reviewer's players and the quality tests cover them, and idle play never loses.
